summary: Today’s pulse tracks Yemen's government announces all-out war to reclaim land from Houthis, Israel condemns Green party passing ‘Zionism is racism’ as a ‘stain on history of UK’ – UK politics live, and Christa Pike's prognosis still unclear after failed execution, lawyer says. Across BBC and Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are party, racism, and zionism. In the background, Russia strikes Kyiv bridge as German chancellor visits Ukraine in show of support and Indian police accused of sexual harassment against journalists at protest keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Yemen's government announces all-out war to reclaim land from Houthis
headlines.description: The Yemeni president's announcement comes amid an exchange of strikes between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition.

headlines.title: Israel condemns Green party passing ‘Zionism is racism’ as a ‘stain on history of UK’ – UK politics live
headlines.description: Party formally adopts policy which equates Zionism with racism, as all Green party votes to adopt policy that equates Zionism with racism On Friday the Times revealed that Katie Lam , the communities secretary, told a meeting in private earlier this year that the state pension system needs a fundamental overhaul. Speaking in June, when she was a frontbencher but not yet in the shadow cabinet, Lam was asked at a meeting with activists if she thought the pensions triple lock was sustainable. She replied: Ultimately I think what we will need in the end is an entirely new pension system. I mean, a baby that is born today has a 20% chance of living to be 100 and I don’t think we can fund one in five people half of their lives, you know, for the first 20 and the last 30 years. But obviously if you are 90 you probably can’t go out and get a job right, so I think you have to be realistic about how you would taper that and bring that in across the population. The fact is, the triple lock and pensions are things that people have contributed to. Conservatives believe that if you have contributed, then you deserve to get your state pension.

headlines.title: Christa Pike's prognosis still unclear after failed execution, lawyer says
headlines.description: Pike's lawyer says doctors are still trying to clear two lethal doses of pentobarbital from her body.

headlines.title: Russia strikes Kyiv bridge as German chancellor visits Ukraine in show of support
headlines.description: Attack shortly after Friedrich Merz arrived on unannounced visit intended to underline Germany’s backing Russia has struck another major bridge in Kyiv as the German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, arrived in the capital in a show of support for Ukraine. A Russian drone hit Kyiv’s key Northern Bridge over the Dnipro River, marking the fourth consecutive day that Russia has targeted bridges used by tens of thousands of residents commuting between the city’s two banks. Video footage showed cars driving across the bridge as the drone plunged into the roadway and exploded in a burst of fire. Two people were injured in the strike, said Kyiv’s mayor, Vitali Klitschko.

headlines.title: Indian police accused of sexual harassment against journalists at protest
headlines.description: The allegations were made after police detained dozens of protesters demanding the resignation of the election chief over changes to voter rolls.

headlines.title: Green party votes to adopt policy that equates Zionism with racism
headlines.description: Motion calling for single Palestinian state, which is opposed by most Green MPs and expected to be challenged, passes by 1,022 votes to 813 UK politics live – latest updates The Greens in England and Wales have formally adopted a policy that equates Zionism with racism and calls for Israel to be replaced by a single Palestinian state. The move is expected to be challenged by some party members under equality laws, with one leading KC saying such a case would have a good chance of succeeding.

headlinePool.description: Cornell president Michael I. Kotlikoff said his university "must do better" in a video statement. "This is a defining moment in Cornell's history," he added.

headlinePool.title: Lions and cheetahs and chimps, oh my: a spotlight on Africa's diverse wildlife
headlinePool.description: Wunmi Mosaku ( Sinners, Loki ) narrates NatGeo's new documentary Africa: Earth's Wild Home

headlinePool.title: Mass shootings leave two people dead in Georgia and 12-year-old girl dead in Baltimore
headlinePool.description: At least 25 injured at block party shooting in Georgia and three wounded in Baltimore park shooting, officials say Two people were killed and at least 25 others injured when a shooting erupted at a homecoming block party in Vienna, Georgia, early on Sunday, according to authorities. In another high-profile mass shooting in the US over the weekend, a 12-year-old girl was shot and killed and three others were wounded after gunfire evidently broke out over a parking spot in a Baltimore park on Saturday, officials said.

headlinePool.title: Egyptian journalist faces terrorism charges after entire newsroom detained
headlinePool.description: Calls for release of six Matsadaash staff after one is charged, while whereabouts of other five remain unknown An Egyptian journalist has been charged with joining a terrorist group, days after an entire newsroom was detained in what rights groups have said is a crackdown on press freedoms. Last week, authorities arrested six journalists from the independent fact-checking and investigative platform Matsadaash – literally meaning “don’t believe” – accusing them in a statement of being unlicensed and publishing false news on behalf of the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood.

headlinePool.title: U.S. Marine arrested for alleged murder of a woman in Okinawa, Japan
headlinePool.description: Japanese police arrested a U.S. Marine in the alleged robbery and murder of a woman on Okinawa, officials said Sunday.

headlinePool.title: More than 400 schools in France to be closed on Monday as more protests planned
headlinePool.description: Education minister says 24 schools have been burnt or ransacked and 78 staff members injured since student unrest began last week Europe live – latest updates More than 400 schools in France will be closed or partly closed on Monday as authorities brace for a second week of student protests. Lessons will be totally or partly suspended in 400 to 500 schools because security conditions “have not been fulfilled”, the education minister, Édouard Geffray, said on Sunday.

headlinePool.title: Nigel Farage questioned by standards commissioner over £5m gift
headlinePool.description: Reform UK leader was interviewed for half an hour last month over money from crypto billionaire Nigel Farage has been interviewed by the standards commissioner for an investigation into whether he should have declared a £5m gift from the crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne. The Reform UK leader spent about half an hour being questioned over the money, the Sunday Times reported. Farage maintains the gift was for his personal security.

headlinePool.title: Thousands of child-on-child sexual offences reported at schools in England and Wales
headlinePool.description: Exclusive: Average of nearly five sexual crimes a day against under-13s were reported to police between 2021 and 2025 From unwanted touching to rape: the scale of child-on-child abuse in English and Welsh schools Lawyers and campaigners have condemned the “horrifying” scale of child-on-child sexual abuse in schools after a Guardian investigation revealed thousands of sexual offences against under-13s, including multiple rapes, are reported to police every year. Close to five sexual crimes against children aged 12 and younger were recorded on average by police every day in primary and secondary schools in England and Wales, according to Guardian analysis of police data for 2021-25.

headlinePool.title: How the Cornell case is affecting women who have experienced sexual assault
headlinePool.description: The rape allegations that have emerged from a Cornell University frat house are leading many women to remember their own experiences — and call for a wider reckoning over sexual violence.
